title: [ORION-QG QG-25] Tropical transfer spectra and asymptotic compiler phases for periodic TARE families
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Required parent: QG-24 finite tropical weighted automaton #880 (no strong QG-25 authority until QG-24 earns exactness for the relevant grammar).
Related parents: QG-8/QG-16 objective phase cones; QG-21 certificate robustness; QG-17R bounded sharpness negative.
Method donors: min-plus/max-plus matrix powers, critical cycle means, eventual periodicity/cyclicity, tropical spectral theory.

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE ASYMPTOTIC COMPILER-PHASE PROGRAMME — freeze before periodic-family execution.**

QG-24 represents an n-qubit six-target TARE instance as a word over the 4096-symbol Pauli-column alphabet. For a frozen periodic target family with motif

`m = x_1 x_2 ... x_L`,

repeated k times, one period induces a finite tropical transfer matrix `M_m` on the exact QG-24 state space (or on each separately frozen global-control sector).

The exact optimum for k repetitions is then a min-plus matrix-power observable of the form

`C_m(k) = alpha ⊗ M_m^k ⊗ beta`,

followed by the finite minimum over frozen global-control sectors.

## Q1 — eventual affine-periodicity

Test and, where the exact tropical spectral hypotheses apply, prove a compiler-specific consequence:

There exist finite integers `K>=0`, `p>=1` and an exact increment `Delta` such that for all `k>=K`,

`C_m(k+p) = C_m(k) + Delta`.

Equivalently the exact optimal cost is eventually affine-periodic in repetition count, and the asymptotic per-motif cost density is `Delta/p`.

Do not assume irreducibility of the transfer graph. The checker must identify the reachable/co-reachable critical components actually controlling `alpha M^k beta`, or return an honest reducible-case partial result.

## Q2 — critical compiler cycles

For each frozen motif, serialize:
- reachable state graph after one motif;
- minimum cycle mean among accepting-relevant components;
- one exact critical cycle witness;
- transient K and period p when machine-checkable;
- exact direct costs for a pre-frozen prefix of k values as controls.

Interpret a critical cycle only as a repeating **compiler-state mechanism**, not a physical phase.

## Q3 — objective-indexed asymptotic phases

Lift transition weights to the existing linear objective coordinates where valid. Each cycle has an exact average resource vector, hence an affine cycle-mean cost in objective space.

Freeze a rational objective slice before opening results and determine which critical cycle is globally minimal on each cell.

Candidate compiler-specific science:
- exact asymptotic regime cells indexed by critical compiler cycles;
- codimension-1 tie surfaces where two asymptotic mechanisms exchange dominance;
- codimension-2 or higher multicritical points where >=3 critical cycles tie;
- comparison with QG-8/QG-16 certificate facets without assuming they coincide.

Generic tropical/normal-fan geometry receives zero novelty credit; only the TARE-specific cycle/resource structure is candidate contribution.

## Q4 — first periodic subjects

Before execution freeze a small, non-adaptive subject panel such as:
1. unary motifs (one Pauli-column type repeated);
2. two-column alternating motifs selected from exact n=1/n=2 TARE controls;
3. at least one motif whose columns realize the QG-7f overlapping comm-s2 support pattern;
4. one neutral control expected to remain in the donor/D+ regime.

No post-outcome motif cherry-picking in V1.

## Q5 — finite-to-asymptotic crossover

Measure whether the finite-k optimal mechanism differs from the eventual critical cycle. Serialize the first crossover index and all exact ties.

A long transient is a positive scientific result: it shows why small-n regime observations can misidentify asymptotic compiler behavior.

## Q6 — relationship to robustness

On a frozen objective trajectory, combine QG-21 certificate margins with critical-cycle tie surfaces:
- theorem cone gives a lower bound on where an existing normal-form proof remains valid;
- exact asymptotic cycle exchange gives an asymptotic mechanism boundary;
- equality may be called an asymptotic true boundary only for the frozen periodic family after complete transfer-state exactness is established.

Do not promote this to a global finite-instance phase boundary.

## Independent generic ORION

Generic ORION must independently build the motif transfer relation from the QG-24 state contract, compute critical cycle means/cyclicity, and reproduce the exact scalar sequence on the frozen k-prefix.

## Native ORION-Q

Keep distinct:
- `ASYMPTOTIC_AFFINE_PERIODICITY`;
- `CRITICAL_COMPILER_CYCLE`;
- `ASYMPTOTIC_PHASE_BOUNDARY_PERIODIC_FAMILY`;
- `FINITE_INSTANCE_GLOBAL_PHASE_BOUNDARY`;
- `PHYSICAL_PHASE_TRANSITION`.

Only the first three can be considered in QG-25.

## Strong terminals

- `QG25_PERIODIC_TARE_COST_EVENTUALLY_AFFINE_PERIODIC_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG25_ASYMPTOTIC_COMPILER_PHASE_CELLS_FROM_CRITICAL_CYCLES_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG25_MULTICRITICAL_COMPILER_POINT_FOUND_ON_FROZEN_OBJECTIVE_SLICE`

Honest alternatives:
- `QG25_REDUCIBLE_TRANSFER_GRAPH_PARTIAL__CRITICAL_COMPONENT_OPEN`
- `QG25_FINITE_TRANSIENT_EXCEEDS_FROZEN_SEARCH_CAP`
- `QG25_QG24_PARENT_NOT_EXACT`
- `QG25_GENERIC_NATIVE_DISAGREEMENT`
- `QG25_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Claim boundary / donor subtraction

Ultimate periodicity of tropical matrix powers, cycle-mean spectral theory, transfer matrices and tropical phase geometry are donor mathematics. Candidate contribution is only the exact TARE-specific transfer spectrum, critical compiler mechanisms, crossover behavior and periodic-family objective phase structure. No novelty, R6 or physical quantum-advantage authority is requested.
